core: Both communities specifically study agent behavior when task instructions are reversed partway through work: they design trials that insert a mid-task instruction reversal after initial progress, then compare outcomes from before that reversal to after it. Community 1 measures how much prior work gets discarded once the agent adopts the new, reversed objective; community 2 measures whether previously stated constraints are still satisfied once the reversal is introduced. In both cases the reversal scenario is treated as a harder, distinct condition than straightforward single-objective tasks, with performance explicitly tracked as worse under it.
quote_1: worse on multi-turn tasks with instruction reversals than on straightforward single-objective ones
quote_2: an instruction reversal inserted after initial inspection
